findings.body:
**Emit a JSON artifact for health observation errors.**

If `state/runs` exists but cannot be listed, `run_metadata_sample()` raises `PermissionError`. This branch rethrows it. The entrypoint at Line 2255 then exits with prose on stderr and no JSON on stdout, including with `--json`.

Handle health errors with the structured error path. Retain exit code 1 for a thrown observation error.

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty” and stdout must remain “exactly one JSON artifact.”
findings.title: Emit a JSON artifact for health observation errors.

findings.body:
**Hold the runner tick lock from the drain gate through unit start.**

`switch_unit` serializes only against other controller transactions. It takes `effects.controller_lock()` at `deploy-controller.py:1821` and calls `queue_drain_gate(effects, unit)` once, at line 1828. The runner tick does not take that lock. It runs under `state/tick.lock` through `with_lock(tick, ...)` (`crq.py:3975`), which uses `flock` at `crq.py:3703`. Neither `deploy-controller.py` nor `unit-live-binding.py` references `tick.lock`.

After the gate, the transaction continues through snapshot, journal writes, `adapter.stop_and_drain(unit)` and `captured_state` (lines 1842–1843), `install` (1849), and `adapter.start(unit)` (1854). `stop_and_drain` fences only the selected `unit`. Another issuing unit that remains active can run the tick in that interval and dispatch queue work the gate did not observe. A dispatch before `captured_state` enters the baseline. A dispatch after `preservation_check` (1850) and before `start` (1854) is not checked. The post-start completion checks (1855–1856) do not re-read the queue. The record can therefore report `completed` while live queue work exists that the gate never saw.

Hold `state/tick.lock` exclusively across the gate, the install, and the completion checks. Use the same non-blocking `flock` as `with_lock`. Alternatively, stop every other issuing unit before the gate and keep them stopped until start. Either change requires a deliberate choice about tick wait behavior, because `with_lock` gives ticks a 90-second wait and then exits.
findings.title: Hold the runner tick lock from the drain gate through unit start.

findings.body:
**Do not reuse pre-activation digests to authorize post-activation recovery.**

In `switch_unit`, `identity["state"]` is captured at the `drained` phase (`deploy-controller.py:1844-1846`), before `adapter.install` and `adapter.start`. Its `preserved/queue.json` and `preserved/heartbeat.json` digests describe the bytes before the target runs. When a later step fails after start, the rollback branch calls `adapter.restore` and then `preservation_check(effects, identity["state"], preserved_surfaces(unit))` at lines 1873-1875. A completed tick of an issuing unit rewrites `queue.json` or `heartbeat.json`, so that check raises `Refused`. The inner `except` turns this into `RecoveryRequired` with outcome `recovery_required`. `restore_activation` does not run.

`recover_unit()` repeats the same comparison at lines 1521-1522 with `record["state"]`, the stale value copied from the journal. It does not re-capture state before the check, so each retry fails the same way after the target has written its surfaces.

Keep the byte-preservation check before activation (lines 1850-1851), where it guards the installation. For the post-activation rollback and recovery paths, do not compare the surfaces that the target legitimately writes against the pre-activation snapshot. Define the evidence that replaces this comparison before changing the branch. A correct replacement depends on what the restore must protect, which this code does not state.
findings.title: Do not reuse pre-activation digests to authorize post-activation recovery.
